provenance: Assess-and-classify tables for the sick young infant from birth up to 2 months, following the WHO/UNICEF Integrated Management of Newborn and Childhood Illness chart booklet and the WHO guidance on managing possible serious bacterial infection in young infants. The signs and thresholds in the possible-serious-bacterial-infection row are deliberately identical to the PSBI_YOUNG_INFANT danger-sign rule in paediatric-danger-signs.json: the alert layer and the classification layer must never disagree about the same baby. Thresholds and wording are an engineering seed and are NOT a ratified national protocol. They require MoHCC and neonatal specialist sign-off before they drive care. See docs/clinical-governance/edliz-engineering-seed-policy.md.

tables.name: Possible serious bacterial infection
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI chart booklet — sick young infant age up to 2 months
WHO — managing possible serious bacterial infection in young infants

tiers.name: Possible serious bacterial infection or very severe disease
tiers.action: Give the first dose of injectable antibiotics, keep the infant warm, treat hypoglycaemia, and refer urgently to hospital with the mother.
treatments: First dose of injectable ampicillin and gentamicin per EDLIZ neonatal dosing
Advise the mother to keep breastfeeding

tiers.name: Local bacterial infection
tiers.action: Give an oral antibiotic for 5 days, teach the mother to treat local infections at home, and review in 2 days.
treatments: Oral amoxicillin for 5 days per EDLIZ neonatal dosing
Teach the mother to treat the umbilicus or pustules at home

tiers.name: Severe disease or local infection unlikely
tiers.action: No antibiotic. Advise the mother on home care for the young infant and teach the signs that mean return immediately.
treatments: Home care for the young infant

testCases.name: poor feeding is possible serious bacterial infection
hypothermia is possible serious bacterial infection
60 breaths a minute is possible serious bacterial infection in a young infant
a red umbilicus without spread is a local infection
a fully assessed well infant is unlikely to have either
an infant with no temperature and no respiratory rate cannot be cleared

tables.name: Jaundice
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI chart booklet — jaundice in the young infant

tiers.name: Severe jaundice
tiers.action: Treat to prevent low blood sugar, keep the infant warm, and refer urgently to hospital. Jaundice in the first 24 hours, yellow palms or soles, or jaundice persisting beyond 14 days all need investigation the same day.
treatments: Urgent referral for bilirubin assessment and phototherapy

tiers.name: Jaundice
tiers.action: Advise the mother on home care, encourage frequent breastfeeding, and review in 1 day. Tell her to return immediately if the palms or soles become yellow.
treatments: Return immediately if palms or soles turn yellow

testCases.name: jaundice in the first 24 hours is severe
yellow palms are severe at any age
jaundice still present at 16 days is severe
day-three jaundice with normal palms is jaundice
an infant never looked at for jaundice is not clear of it

tables.name: Diarrhoea in the young infant
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI chart booklet — diarrhoea in the young infant

tiers.name: Severe dehydration
tiers.action: Start Plan C now — intravenous fluid if you can give it — and refer urgently. A young infant dehydrates faster than an older child and tolerates it less well.

tiers.name: Some dehydration
tiers.action: Give ORS at this facility under observation (Plan B), continue breastfeeding throughout, and reassess.

tiers.name: No dehydration
tiers.action: Continue breastfeeding and give extra fluid (Plan A). Teach the mother the signs that mean return immediately.
treatments: Plan A — continue and increase breastfeeding

testCases.name: sunken eyes with a very slow skin pinch is severe
no diarrhoea means the table does not apply
one sign with the rest unexamined cannot be called no dehydration

tables.name: Feeding problem or low weight for age
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI chart booklet — feeding problem or low weight in the young infant

tiers.name: Feeding problem or low weight for age
tiers.action: Counsel the mother on positioning and attachment, treat thrush if present, and review in 2 days. A low weight for age in a young infant is a feeding problem until proven otherwise.
treatments: Counsel on correct positioning and attachment
Advise breastfeeding at least 8 times in 24 hours
Treat oral thrush with nystatin if present

tiers.name: No feeding problem
tiers.action: Praise the mother for feeding the infant well and advise her to continue exclusive breastfeeding.
treatments: Praise and encourage continued exclusive breastfeeding

testCases.name: poor attachment is a feeding problem
low weight for age alone is a feeding problem
feeding well and growing is no feeding problem
an infant who was never weighed cannot be cleared
